content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/chiragnvijay/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/superpowers/6.4.1/skills/brainstorming

# Brainstorming Ideas Into Designs

Help turn ideas into fully formed designs and specs through natural collaborative dialogue.

Start by classifying how much process the request needs, then work
through your path: understand the context, refine the idea, present a
design, and get your human partner's approval.

## Establish Shared Understanding

The outcome of brainstorming is an understanding your human partner can
recognize and correct, grounded in what they want to accomplish.

1. **Discover intent.** Use the request and available context to identify
   the intended outcome, who it is for, and what success looks like. When
   that information is missing, ask one focused question about purpose or
   intended use before proposing features or an approach. Knowing the app
   genre does not tell you why your partner wants it. Gathering missing
   requirements does not ask them to authorize the task again.
2. **Write back your understanding.** Summarize the intended outcome,
   relevant constraints, and success criteria in a short note your partner
   can assess. Separate what they said from assumptions. Invite correction
   and incorporate their answer before treating this as the design brief.
3. **Carry intent into the design.** Preserve the agreed understanding in
   the selected path's design artifact: the written spec for architectural
   work, or the in-chat design/probe for bounded work and spikes. Check
   proposed features and technical choices against that understanding.

When the request already supplies the purpose and constraints, reflect
that understanding instead of asking the same questions again. Keep the
note concise; its accuracy and the opportunity to correct it matter.

<HARD-GATE>
Before taking any implementation action, including invoking an
implementation skill, writing product code, scaffolding, installing
product dependencies, or creating an external project, complete the
selected path's prerequisites:

- Spike: the human partner approves the question and probe.
- Bounded: the human partner approves the short in-chat design.
- Architectural: the human partner reviews and approves the written spec,
  then reviews the written implementation plan and selects its execution
  method. Conversational design approval only permits writing the spec;
  written-spec approval only permits invoking writing-plans.

A reply approves the stage actually presented. Approval of an idea or
feature scope does not approve artifacts that do not exist yet. Resume
at the earliest incomplete stage; do not turn one approval into permission
to skip the rest of the selected path. Read-only project exploration is
allowed while those prerequisites remain incomplete.
</HARD-GATE>

## Three Paths

Before your first question, classify the request and say the
classification out loud — "this looks bounded, so I'll present a short
design here rather than write a spec" — so your human partner can
override it:

- **Spike** — a feasibility question ("can we...", "is it possible...",
  "quick and dirty is fine") whose output is an answer, not code you
  keep. Present the question and what you'll try in 2-3 sentences, get
  a nod, then find out as cheaply as correctness allows. No design
  doc, no spec file. Report findings as a recommendation; anything you
  built stays labeled throwaway.
- **Bounded** — a well-scoped change to code that already exists in
  this repo: a new flag, a small endpoint, a one-file fix.
  Understanding the kind of app is not enough — bounded means the flow
  you are changing is already here to read. If there is no existing
  flow to change, the task is not bounded. Ask the clarifying
  questions that matter, present a short design IN CHAT (a few
  sentences to a few short paragraphs), and STOP. Implementation
  starts only after your human partner says yes to that design — a
  bounded task's approval is as hard a gate as an architectural
  one. No spec file, no implementation plan document.
- **Architectural** — new projects, new subsystems, changes that
  restructure how components fit together or alter interfaces others
  depend on. Follow the full process: questions, approaches, sectioned
  design, written spec, then the writing-plans skill.

When in doubt between two paths, take the heavier one. The ratchet is
one-way: hidden complexity discovered mid-task upgrades the path —
stop, say so, and step up. Nothing downgrades mid-task.

## Anti-Pattern: "Too Simple To Need Approval"

Every path ends with your human partner approving the required design
before implementation. A bounded change may need only two sentences in
chat. A new todo-list project is architectural and requires the written
spec and planning handoffs. Scale the artifact to the selected path;
complete that path's reviews before implementation.

## Red Flags

| Thought | Reality |
|---------|---------|
| "This is too simple to need a design" | Follow the selected path: a bounded change gets a short chat design; an architectural change gets the written spec and planning handoffs. |
| "I'll call it bounded and skip the spec" | Reaching for a label to skip work IS the doubt — take the heavier path. |
| "It's bounded and the design is obvious — I'll start while they read it" | The gate is the approval, not the design's length. Present, then stop until you hear yes. |
| "I understand this kind of app, so it's bounded" | Bounded measures the repo, not your familiarity. A new project has no existing flow — it is architectural. |
| "The spike works, so I'll keep the code" | A spike's output is an answer. Keeping the code is a new request — classify it. |
| "It grew, but I'm almost done — no need to re-classify" | Hidden complexity upgrades the path mid-task. Stop and say so. |
| "They approved the spike, so the follow-up change is approved too" | Each task gets its own classification and its own approval. |

## Checklist

Classify first, announce the path, then create a task for each item on
your path and complete them in order.

**Spike:**
1. **Explore project context** — enough to frame the probe
2. **Present question + probe plan** — 2-3 sentences
3. **Get approval** — a nod is enough
4. **Investigate** — as cheaply as correctness allows
5. **Report findings** — a recommendation; label anything built as throwaway

**Bounded:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, the ones that matter
3. **Present short design in chat** — approach, files touched, testing
4. **Get approval** — STOP and wait for an explicit yes; presenting the design and starting in the same breath is skipping the gate
5. **Implement** — proceed with the normal development workflow (TDD applies); no plan document

**Architectural:**
1. **Explore project context** — check files, docs, recent commits
2. **Offer the visual companion just-in-time** — NOT upfront. The first time a question would genuinely be clearer shown than described, offer it then (its own message); on approval its browser tab opens for you. If no visual question ever arises, never offer it. See the Visual Companion section below.
3. **Ask clarifying questions** — one at a time, understand purpose/constraints/success criteria
4. **Propose 2-3 approaches** — with trade-offs and your recommendation
5. **Present design** — in sections scaled to their complexity, get user approval after each section
6. **Write design doc** — save to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md` and commit
7. **Spec self-review** — quick inline check for placeholders, contradictions, ambiguity, scope (see below)
8. **User reviews written spec** — ask user to review the spec file before proceeding
9. **Transition to implementation** — invoke writing-plans skill to create implementation plan

## Process Flow

```dot
digraph brainstorming {
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" [shape=diamond];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [shape=box];
    "Present short design in chat" [shape=box];
    "Human approves?" [shape=diamond];
    "Investigate; report recommendation" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Explore project context" [shape=box];
    "Ask clarifying questions" [shape=box];
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" [shape=box];
    "Present design sections" [shape=box];
    "User approves design?" [shape=diamond];
    "Write design doc" [shape=box];
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" [shape=box];
    "User reviews spec?" [shape=diamond];
    "Invoke writing-plans skill" [shape=doublecircle];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" [shape=box];

    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" [label="spike"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" [label="bounded"];
    "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural" -> "Explore project context" [label="architectural"];
    "Present question + probe (2-3 sentences)" -> "Human approves?";
    "Ask clarifying questions (bounded)" -> "Present short design in chat";
    "Present short design in chat" -> "Human approves?";
    "Human approves?" -> "Investigate; report recommendation" [label="spike: yes"];
    "Human approves?" -> "Implement via normal workflow (no plan doc)" [label="bounded: yes"];
    "Hidden complexity? Upgrade path" -> "Classify: spike / bounded / architectural";
    "Explore project context" -> "Ask clarifying questions";
    "Ask clarifying questions" -> "Propose 2-3 approaches";
    "Propose 2-3 approaches" -> "Present design sections";
    "Present design sections" -> "User approves design?";
    "User approves design?" -> "Present design sections" [label="no, revise"];
    "User approves design?" -> "Write design doc" [label="yes"];
    "Write design doc" -> "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)";
    "Spec self-review\n(fix inline)" -> "User reviews spec?";
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Write design doc" [label="changes requested"];
    "User reviews spec?" -> "Invoke writing-plans skill" [label="approved"];
}
```

**Terminal states are path-bound.** Architectural: the ONLY skill you
invoke after brainstorming is writing-plans — never frontend-design,
mcp-builder, or any other implementation skill. Bounded: after
approval, implementation proceeds directly through the normal
development workflow; no plan document. Spike: the terminal state is a
reported recommendation.

## The Process

The subsections below serve the bounded and architectural paths (a
spike stops at "present the probe, get a nod"). Sections from
**Exploring approaches** onward are architectural-path depth — for
bounded work, context plus a few questions plus a short in-chat design
is the whole process.

**Understanding the idea:**

- Check out the current project state first (files, docs, recent commits)
- Before asking detailed questions, assess scope: if the request describes multiple independent subsystems (e.g., "build a platform with chat, file storage, billing, and analytics"), flag this immediately. Don't spend questions refining details of a project that needs to be decomposed first.
- If the project is too large for a single spec, help the user decompose into sub-projects: what are the independent pieces, how do they relate, what order should they be built? Then brainstorm the first sub-project through the normal design flow. Each sub-project gets its own spec → plan → implementation cycle.
- For appropriately-scoped projects, ask questions one at a time to refine the idea
- Prefer multiple choice questions when possible, but open-ended is fine too
- Only one question per message - if a topic needs more exploration, break it into multiple questions
- Focus on understanding: purpose, constraints, success criteria

**Exploring approaches:**

- Propose 2-3 different approaches with trade-offs
- Present options conversationally with your recommendation and reasoning
- Lead with your recommended option and explain why
- YAGNI ruthlessly - remove unnecessary features from every approach and design

**Presenting the design:**

- Once you believe you understand what you're building, present the design
- Scale each section to its complexity: a few sentences if straightforward, up to 200-300 words if nuanced
- Ask after each section whether it looks right so far
- Cover: architecture, components, data flow, error handling, testing
- Be ready to go back and clarify if something doesn't make sense

**Design for isolation and clarity:**

- Break the system into smaller units that each have one clear purpose, communicate through well-defined interfaces, and can be understood and tested independently
- For each unit, you should be able to answer: what does it do, how do you use it, and what does it depend on?
- Can someone understand what a unit does without reading its internals? Can you change the internals without breaking consumers? If not, the boundaries need work.
- Smaller, well-bounded units are also easier for you to work with - you reason better about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. When a file grows large, that's often a signal that it's doing too much.

**Working in existing codebases:**

- Explore the current structure before proposing changes. Follow existing patterns.
- Where existing code has problems that affect the work (e.g., a file that's grown too large, unclear boundaries, tangled responsibilities), include targeted improvements as part of the design - the way a good developer improves code they're working in.
- Don't propose unrelated refactoring. Stay focused on what serves the current goal.

## After the Design (architectural path)

**Documentation:**

- Write the validated design (spec) to `docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`
  - (User preferences for spec location override this default)
- Use elements-of-style:writing-clearly-and-concisely skill if available
- Commit the design document to git

**Spec Self-Review:**
After writing the spec document, look at it with fresh eyes:

1. **Placeholder scan:** Any "TBD", "TODO", incomplete sections, or vague requirements? Fix them.
2. **Internal consistency:** Do any sections contradict each other? Does the architecture match the feature descriptions?
3. **Scope check:** Is this focused enough for a single implementation plan, or does it need decomposition?
4. **Ambiguity check:** Could any requirement be interpreted two different ways? If so, pick one and make it explicit.

Fix any issues inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on.

**User Review Gate:**
After the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:

> "Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan."

Wait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.

**Implementation:**

- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan
- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.

## Visual Companion

A browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.

**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:
> "This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you."

**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. Wait for the user's response. If they accept, start the server with `--open` so their browser opens to the first screen automatically. If they decline, continue text-only and don't offer again unless they raise it.

**Per-question decision:** Even after the user accepts, decide FOR EACH QUESTION whether to use the browser or the terminal. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**

- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs
- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions

A question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. "What does personality mean in this context?" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. "Which wizard layout works better?" is a visual question — use the browser.

If they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:
`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`

# BMW Product Decision Studio

Feature decisions for the BMW 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60) and 7 Series (G70), traced to the data in `BMW-Data/`: 10,128 customer comments, the 2025 customer studies (CN/EU and US), sales volumes 2024–2030 and the German price lists (July 2026).

A PM types a feature idea ("seat massage", "climate control", "vacuum for pet hair"). The system answers per series and market with **Prioritise / Consider / Low priority / Insufficient evidence / Not sold**. Every answer carries:
- the evidence behind it: complaint verdict, breadth, unmet requests, survey weakness, sales volume;
- a suggested move taken from the price lists: fix standard equipment, make an option standard, or introduce an item another series already lists;
- comment IDs, survey rows and PDF page references for every number.

Weights and market emphasis are an explicit, hashed policy. Two PMs using the same policy and data get the same answer, and a PM override is logged with its rationale.

```
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # http://127.0.0.1:8000
```

The full analysis is in **[reports/REPORT.md](reports/REPORT.md)**.

---

## Quick start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
# put the hackathon files in BMW-Data/ (git-ignored)

python -m bmw_feedback all            # build + train + figures (~6 min)
cd frontend && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
python -m bmw_feedback serve          # API + web app on http://127.0.0.1:8000

python -m pytest tests -q             # API checks against the processed tables and the PDFs
```

For frontend development, run `npm run dev` in `frontend/` (port 5173). It proxies `/api` to the server on port 8000.

Command-line access works without the app:

```bash
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --feature "head-up display"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --text "The wireless charger keeps overheating my phone"
python -m bmw_feedback verdict --list
```

## The web app

| Page | What it answers |
|---|---|
| Evaluate an idea | Which features the idea matches, then a series × market matrix. Each cell has a recommendation and an evidence panel (signals, weights, reasons, quotes, comment IDs, survey rows, price-list items). Also shows the price ladder across series, an adjustable decision policy, and a form to record the decision. |
| Feature verdicts | All 224 feedback features: channel-adjusted complaint index with 95% CI, verdict, and price-list fitment per series (■ standard, □ optional) |
| Price lists | All three PDFs parsed cell by cell: variants with base price and power, standard and optional equipment per variant with prices and page references, and technical data |
| Markets | Sales by market, how well feedback covers each market, and which customer studies exist |
| Method & audit | Scoring method, classifier metrics, what the price lists changed in the models, complaint drivers, and data-quality checks |
| Decision log | Every accepted or overridden recommendation, with policy and data hashes |

Design: the BMW corporate web system (white canvas, #262626 ink, #1c69d4 for actions only, #1a2129 dark bands, square corners, no shadows). BMW Type Next is licensed, so Barlow (SIL OFL, self-hosted) stands in for it. No BMW logo files are used.

## Pipeline

```
BMW-Data/*.xlsx, *.PDF
   │  load.py            feedback, CN/EU + US surveys, sales volumes
   │  option_catalog.py  price-list PDFs: variants, base prices, ■/□ fitment per variant, option prices,
   │                     packages, technical data; validated on every build
   ▼
clean.py                 one row per comment + one row per label; strip label leakage and templates
taxonomy.py              11 domains ← 224 features ← 84 reasons; survey and price-list link maps
scoring.py               channel-adjusted complaint / praise / request indices with 95% intervals → verdict
classifier.py            TF-IDF + logistic regression: comment → type, domain, feature
                         (+ price-list fitment re-ranker when the car is known)
risk_model.py            explainable boosting machine: what drives complaints (glass box)
decision.py              idea → features → per series × market recommendation + suggested move
api.py                   FastAPI; serves frontend/dist
```

### What the price lists feed

The PDFs are parsed from glyph and text positions, not from text order. Every build checks that:
- all 1,889 ■/□ marks on the 32 table pages land in a variant column;
- all 1,128 option prices and 23 base prices satisfy gross = net × 1.19;
- power on the price pages matches the technical data for all 23 variants.

One printed anomaly (F70 p.17) is kept as printed. 106 feedback features are linked to price-list items through a curated keyword map, and each link shows the keyword that produced it.

| Layer | Use of the price lists | Measured effect |
|---|---|---|
| Feature classifier | Re-ranks candidates by the feature's fitment on the comment's car | +0.6 pp top-1 on comments about linked features (26 fixed, 4 broken, McNemar p = 0.0001) |
| Complaint model | Fitment tier, option price and % of base price as inputs | No held-out gain (AUC −0.0008, feature-grouped CV), so the production model uses context only; the price-list variant is kept for audit |
| Decision engine | Price ladder across series, standard vs optional vs not listed, suggested move | Deterministic, with page references |

## Outputs

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `reports/REPORT.md` | Findings, method, roadmap |
| `reports/model_ablation.json` | Price-list ablations for both models, EBM shape functions |
| `reports/classifier_metrics.json`, `data_quality.json` | Classifier CV metrics, cleaning and PDF-validation counts |
| `data/processed/catalog_*.csv` | Parsed price lists: variants, items, fitment, packages, technical data, feature links |
| `data/decisions.jsonl` | Decision log written by the app (git-ignored) |

```
bmw_feedback/     pipeline package and API
frontend/         React + Vite web app (built into frontend/dist)
tests/            API and pipeline checks
reports/          report, figures, scorecards, metrics
BMW-Data/         raw hackathon data (not committed)
```

"""Feature-idea decision engine: one PM question in, a traceable per-market answer out.

    idea text -> matched VFC features (alias / name / text classifier, PM confirms)
              -> per (model, market) cell: four evidence signals in [0, 1]
              -> weighted score -> Prioritise / Consider / Low priority
              -> action type from the DE price list (fix, make standard, introduce)

Signals (each cites its source rows; a missing signal is shown, never imputed)
    complaints  channel-adjusted complaint verdict of the feature in that model + market
    breadth     how many of the model's customers raise the feature at all (percentile)
    requests    channel-adjusted request index ('Wants') in that model + market
    survey      how weak the matching survey attribute is in that model + market (percentile)

Weights, market multipliers and thresholds are policy, not data: they live in
DEFAULT_POLICY, are returned with every result and hashed, so two PMs with the
same policy and data get the same answer and an override is visible.
"""

import copy
import hashlib
import json
import re

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from . import config, scoring, taxonomy
from .verdict import load_catalog, load_context

MARKETS = ["EU", "US", "CN", "RoW"]
MARKET_NAMES = {"EU": "Europe", "US": "United States", "CN": "China", "RoW": "Rest of world"}
SALES_GROUP = {"F70": "F70", "G60": "G60_G68", "G70": "G70"}
CN_SURVEY_MODEL = {"G60": "G68", "G70": "G70"}       # the CN survey covers the long-wheelbase G68, not G60

DEFAULT_POLICY = {
    "version": "1.0",
    "weights": {"complaints": 0.4, "breadth": 0.2, "requests": 0.2, "survey": 0.2},
    "market_multipliers": {"EU": 1.0, "US": 1.0, "CN": 1.0, "RoW": 1.0},
    "volume_year": 2025,
    "thresholds": {"prioritise": 0.6, "consider": 0.35, "min_coverage": 0.5},
    "borrowing": {"enabled": True, "discount": 0.5, "into_cn": False},
    # Fixed mappings from evidence to signal points (not editable in the UI, but hashed and shown)
    "scoring": {
        "complaint_points": {"Bad": 1.0, "Leaning bad": 0.67, "Mixed": 0.33, "Leaning good": 0.0, "Good": 0.0},
        "request_points": {"requested": 1.0, "index_at_least": config.LEAN_BAD_INDEX, "elevated": 0.5, "otherwise": 0.0},
        "min_comments_for_signal": config.MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_VERDICT,
        "survey_weakness": "(rank - 1) / (attributes - 1); rank 1 = best-rated attribute of that series in that market",
        "breadth": "percentile of the feature's comment count among the series' features (all markets)",
    },
    "rationale": {
        "weights": "Complaints weigh twice as much as requests (PM guidance: complaints and defects outrank "
                   "wish-list features). Breadth rewards features many customers raise over niche ones.",
        "market_multipliers": "1.0 = market weighted by its sales volume. Raise a market to emphasise it "
                              "(e.g. a regional strategy); lower to de-emphasise.",
        "thresholds": "A cell needs at least half of the weighted evidence present to get a recommendation.",
        "borrowing": "When a model + market has fewer than 8 comments on the feature, the model's verdict over "
                     "all markets is used at a discounted weight and labelled 'borrowed'. China has no customer "
                     "feedback in the data and configurations differ by market, so it does not borrow by default.",
    },
}
SIGNALS = ["complaints", "breadth", "requests", "survey"]


def _hash(obj) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, default=str).encode()).hexdigest()[:12]


def data_fingerprint() -> dict:
    """Content hash of every raw input file, so a decision can be tied to the exact data."""
    files = sorted(config.RAW_DIR.glob("*"))
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    listing = []
    for f in files:
        if f.is_file():
            digest = hashlib.sha256(f.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
            h.update(f.name.encode() + digest.encode())
            listing.append({"file": f.name, "sha256": digest[:12], "bytes": f.stat().st_size})
    return {"hash": h.hexdigest()[:12], "files": listing}


def policy_hash(policy: dict) -> str:
    """Hash of everything that changes a score: weights, multipliers, thresholds, year, borrowing, scoring, version."""
    return _hash({k: policy[k] for k in ("version", "weights", "market_multipliers", "thresholds", "volume_year",
                                         "borrowing", "scoring")})


def merge_policy(overrides: dict | None) -> dict:
    policy = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_POLICY)
    for key in ("weights", "market_multipliers", "thresholds"):
        for k, v in ((overrides or {}).get(key) or {}).items():
            if k in policy[key] and v is not None:
                policy[key][k] = float(v)
    b = (overrides or {}).get("borrowing") or {}
    if "enabled" in b:
        policy["borrowing"]["enabled"] = bool(b["enabled"])
    if "into_cn" in b:
        policy["borrowing"]["into_cn"] = bool(b["into_cn"])
    if b.get("discount") is not None:
        policy["borrowing"]["discount"] = min(max(float(b["discount"]), 0.0), 1.0)
    if (overrides or {}).get("volume_year") in (2024, 2025, 2030):
        policy["volume_year"] = int(overrides["volume_year"])
    return policy


class DecisionEngine:
    def __init__(self, ctx=None):
        self.ctx = ctx or load_context()

options.label: Flag only

content.text:
Scope is settled. Luna handles the retriever and verifier, and Terra writes the explanation. Here are the approaches, then the first design section.

## Approaches

**A. Engine-grounded fact bundle (recommended).**
- The graph is built offline from the processed tables and model outputs.
- **Retriever:** gathers candidates without an LLM (aliases, the TF-IDF classifier, embeddings of graph nodes). Luna then picks among those candidate IDs to fill a Pydantic `IdeaSpec`. Validators reject anything not in the graph, and you confirm the result.
- **Numbers:** the existing `DecisionEngine` computes every one. They're packed into a `FactBundle`, where each fact has a stable ID and a provenance pointer into the graph.
- **Explainer (Terra):** writes claims that may only cite fact IDs from that bundle.
- **Verifier:** a deterministic check first, then Luna for purely semantic claims. Failures go back for one rewrite, then get stripped.
- **Why recommended:** the LLM never computes a number, which makes "based on actual data" checkable.

**B. Graph-RAG with tool calling.** The agents run a tool loop over graph queries (`neighbors`, `feature_stats`, …) and explore on their own. It's more "agentic" and flexible. But it isn't deterministic, uses more tokens and takes longer. It's also harder to verify, because the LLM can combine or recompute numbers on the way.

**C. Neo4j + LLM-written Cypher.** A real graph database with text-to-query. It means heavy infrastructure (a Docker server) and query-generation errors. That's overkill for about 15k nodes.

## Section 1: Architecture and knowledge graph (assumes A)

```
build time   processed CSVs + models/ + reports/*.json
               └─ graph/build.py ─→ data/processed/knowledge_graph.json (networkx node-link)
                                   graph_schema.json (node/edge types + counts)
                                   graph_embeddings.npy (OpenAI embeddings of feature/reason/option/survey text)
request time idea ─→ Retriever (Luna) ─→ IdeaSpec ─→ PM confirms
                     ─→ DecisionEngine (unchanged maths) ─→ FactBundle + evidence subgraph   [renders immediately]
                     ─→ Explainer (Terra) ─→ Verifier (rules + Luna) ─→ retry once ─→ strip  [fills in]
```

**Node types.** Every node has a stable ID and a provenance pointer (`table`, `key`) or (`file`, `page`).

| Group | Nodes (ID pattern) | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Product | `Series` (3), `Variant` (23, power + base price), `TechSpec` (556), `OptionItem` (365, SA code, page), `Package` (98) | catalog_*.csv / PDFs |
| Market | `Market` (4), `SalesVolume` (series × market × year) | sales.csv |
| Feedback | `Domain` (11), `Feature` (224), `Reason` (84), `Comment` (~10k) | taxonomy, labels.csv, comments.csv |
| Survey | `SurveyAttribute`, `SurveyScore` (attribute × market × series, mean or top-2-box + rank) | survey_*.csv |
| Model outputs | `VerdictCell` (feature × series × market: indices, 95% CI, verdict), `ModelArtifact` (3 classifiers, complaint EBM, fitment re-ranker, with metrics), `EBMTerm` (global importance + per-level contribution), `Caveat` (DE-only prices, no China feedback, CN survey = G68, G70 tables cover 4 of 7 variants, no AUC gain from PDF fitment) | scoring, reports/*.json, models/ |

**Edges:**
- Feature `IN_DOMAIN` Domain.
- Comment `MENTIONS {sentiment, type, reason}` Feature.
- Comment `ABOUT` Series and `FROM` Market.
- Feature `LINKED_TO {keyword}` OptionItem.
- OptionItem `FITTED_ON {standard|optional, €}` Variant.
- Variant `OF` Series.
- Feature `HAS_SPEC` TechSpec.
- SurveyAttribute `MEASURES` Feature.
- Series `SOLD_IN` Market (via SalesVolume).
- VerdictCell `SCORES` Feature / Series / Market.
- Unlabelled Comment `PREDICTED_AS {p}` Feature, from the feature classifier.
- EBMTerm `EXPLAINS` Domain / Series / Market.
- Caveat `QUALIFIES` whatever it limits.

The build asserts node counts against the source tables (224 features, 11 domains, 23 variants, 1,889 fitment marks, …) and fails loudly on any mismatch. Without a key, embeddings fall back to TF-IDF so the build still runs offline.

Does this approach and graph structure look right? Anything missing from how features, feedback, price, specs, sales and model outputs should connect?

"""PM-facing verdict cards: 'is this feature good or bad, and why?'

Two entry points:
    feature_card(name)  -> verdict for a feature that already has feedback
    text_card(comment)  -> classify a new comment, then show the verdict for
                           the feature(s) it is about
"""

import difflib
import re

import pandas as pd

from . import config, scoring

ALIASES = {
    "hud": "Head-Up Display", "head up": "Head-Up Display", "carplay": "Apple CarPlay",
    "android": "Android Auto", "idrive": "Operating concept, operating system",
    "infotainment": "ConnectedDrive and Infotainment, overall technology", "screen": "Touch screen, operation",

    "air conditioning": "Vehicle, climatization", "hvac": "Vehicle, climatization", "sunroof": "Panorama glass roof",
    "panoramic roof": "Panorama glass roof", "range": "Electric Range", "charging": "Charge high-voltage battery",
    "key": "Vehicle key", "start stop": "Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA)",
    "start-stop": "Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA)", "ipa": "Intelligent Personal Assistant",
    "voice assistant": "Intelligent Personal Assistant", "app": "My BMW App / MINI App",
    "my bmw app": "My BMW App / MINI App", "esim": "Personal eSIM", "cruise control": "(Active) cruise control",
    "acc": "(Active) cruise control", "parking": "Parking Assistant", "camera": "Rear view camera",
    "wireless charging": "Mobile device, wireless charging", "sound system": "Audio mode, sound",
    "speakers": "Audio mode, sound", "massage": "Seat massage", "doors": "Door, open / close",
    "automatic doors": "Automatic doors", "trunk": "Trunk lid, open / close", "boot": "Luggage compartment",
    "gearbox": "Transmission", "brakes": "Braking", "seats": "Seats", "ota": "Remote Software Upgrade/RSU",
    "software update": "Remote Software Upgrade/RSU", "manual": "Owner's Manual",
}


class Context:
    """Everything a verdict needs, computed once."""

    def __init__(self, labels: pd.DataFrame, comments: pd.DataFrame, survey_us_summary=None, catalog=None):
        self.labels, self.comments = labels, comments
        self.features = scoring.score(labels).set_index("feature")
        self.domains = scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("domain",), prior_keys=()).set_index("domain")
        self.by_model = scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("feature", "model")).set_index(["feature", "model"])
        self.by_engine = scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("feature", "engine")).set_index(["feature", "engine"])
        self.survey = (scoring.survey_crosscheck(survey_us_summary) if survey_us_summary is not None
                       else pd.DataFrame())
        self.catalog = catalog or {}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ lookup
    def resolve(self, query: str):
        """Map a free-form feature query to a VFC feature name (or None)."""
        names = list(self.features.index)
        q = query.strip().lower()
        if q in ALIASES:
            return ALIASES[q]
        exact = [n for n in names if n.lower() == q]
        if exact:
            return exact[0]
        contains = [n for n in names if q in n.lower()]
        if contains:
            return max(contains, key=lambda n: self.features.loc[n, "n_comments"])
        close = difflib.get_close_matches(q, [n.lower() for n in names], n=1, cutoff=0.6)
        if close:
            return next(n for n in names if n.lower() == close[0])
        return None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ card
    def feature_card(self, feature: str) -> dict:
        row = self.features.loc[feature]
        domain = row["domain"]
        dom = self.domains.loc[domain]
        card = {
            "feature": feature, "domain": domain, "verdict": row["verdict"], "confidence": row["confidence"],
            "n_comments": int(row["n_comments"]), "is_umbrella_label": bool(row["is_umbrella"]),
            "requested": bool(row["requested"]), "bad_kind": scoring.bad_kind(row),
            "complaint_index": _ci(row, "negative"), "praise_index": _ci(row, "positive"),
            "request_index": _ci(row, "request"),
            "adjusted_mix": {c: round(float(row[f"adj_share_{c}"]), 3) for c in scoring.SENTIMENTS},
            "raw_mix": {c: round(float(row[f"raw_share_{c}"]), 3) for c in scoring.SENTIMENTS},
            "domain_verdict": dom["verdict"], "domain_complaint_index": round(float(dom["index_negative"]), 2),
            "reasons": scoring.reason_breakdown(self.labels, feature),
            "quotes": scoring.representative_quotes(self.labels, self.comments, feature),
            "by_model": _breakdown(self.by_model, feature), "by_engine": _breakdown(self.by_engine, feature),
            "survey": self._survey(feature), "options": self._options(feature), "specs": self._specs(feature),
        }
        card["summary"] = summary_sentence(card)
        return card

    def _survey(self, feature):
        if self.survey.empty:
            return []
        s = self.survey[self.survey["feature"] == feature]
        return [{"attribute": r.survey_attribute, "model": r.model, "top2_box": round(r.top2_box, 3),
                 "bottom3_box": round(r.bottom3_box, 3)} for r in s.itertuples()]

    def _options(self, feature):
        """Price-list fitment per model (DE price list, July 2026, EUR) with the linked items."""
        summary = self.catalog.get("feature_fitment_summary")
        links = self.catalog.get("feature_option_links")
        if summary is None or links is None:
            return []
        out = []
        for r in summary[summary["feature"] == feature].itertuples():
            lk = links[(links["feature"] == feature) & (links["model"] == r.model)]
            out.append({"model": r.model, "tier": r.tier, "n_variants": int(r.n_variants),
                        "n_standard": int(r.n_standard), "n_optional": int(r.n_optional),
                        "price_min_eur": _f(r.price_min_eur), "price_max_eur": _f(r.price_max_eur),
                        "price_pct_of_base": _f(r.price_pct_of_base),
                        "price_item": None if pd.isna(r.price_item) else r.price_item,
                        "price_via_package": None if pd.isna(r.price_via_package) else bool(r.price_via_package),
                        "items": [{"name": x.option_name, "sa_code": None if pd.isna(x.sa_code) else x.sa_code,
                                   "page": int(x.page), "page_type": x.page_type,
                                   "matched_keyword": x.matched_keyword, "matched_in": x.matched_in,
                                   "matched_text": x.matched_text} for x in lk.itertuples()]})
        return out

    def _specs(self, feature):
        specs = self.catalog.get("feature_specs")
        if specs is None:
            return []
        s = specs[specs["feature"] == feature]
        return [{"model": r.model, "variant": r.variant, "attribute": r.attribute, "value": r.value,
                 "page": int(r.page)} for r in s.itertuples()]


def _f(v):
    return None if v is None or pd.isna(v) else round(float(v), 2)


def _ci(row, c):
    return {"index": round(float(row[f"index_{c}"]), 2), "ci_low": round(float(row[f"ci_low_{c}"]), 2),
            "ci_high": round(float(row[f"ci_high_{c}"]), 2), "observed": int(row[f"obs_{c}"]),
            "expected": round(float(row[f"exp_{c}"]), 1)}


def _breakdown(table, feature):
    if feature not in table.index.get_level_values(0):
        return []
    sub = table.loc[feature]
    return [{"group": g, "n_comments": int(r["n_comments"]), "complaint_index": round(float(r["index_negative"]), 2),
             "verdict": r["verdict"]} for g, r in sub.iterrows()]


def summary_sentence(card: dict) -> str:
    """One deterministic paragraph a PM can paste into a ticket."""
    f, v, n = card["feature"], card["verdict"], card["n_comments"]
    ci = card["complaint_index"]
    if v == "Not enough data":
        return (f"{f} has only {n} comment(s): too few for a verdict. Its domain ({card['domain']}) is rated "
                f"'{card['domain_verdict']}' (complaint index {card['domain_complaint_index']}); use that as the prior.")
    pct = round((ci["index"] - 1) * 100)
    direction = f"{abs(pct)}% more" if pct > 0 else f"{abs(pct)}% fewer"
    text = (f"{f} is rated '{v.upper()}' ({card['confidence']} confidence, {n} comments). Customers raise "
            f"{direction} complaints than for comparable features from the same channels "
            f"(complaint index {ci['index']}, 95% CI {ci['ci_low']}-{ci['ci_high']}).")
    pos = card["reasons"]["positive"]["families"]
    neg = card["reasons"]["negative"]["families"]
    req = card["reasons"]["request"]["families"]
    if pos:
        text += f" Praise centres on: {', '.join(list(pos)[:2]).lower()}."
    if neg:
        text += f" Complaints are {card['bad_kind']}, mainly: {', '.join(list(neg)[:2]).lower()}."
    if card["requested"] and req:
        text += f" It is also an unmet need - customers ask for: {', '.join(list(req)[:2]).lower()}."
    if card["is_umbrella_label"]:
        text += " Note: this is an umbrella label; annotators file general praise here, so judge it at domain level."
    return text


def render_markdown(card: dict) -> str:
    """Human-readable card for the terminal."""
    lines = [f"## {card['feature']} -> {card['verdict']}",
             f"*{card['domain']}* | confidence: {card['confidence']} | {card['n_comments']} comments", "",
             card["summary"], ""]
    if card["verdict"] != "Not enough data":
        mix = card["adjusted_mix"]
        lines += [f"Channel-adjusted mix: {mix['positive']:.0%} praise, {mix['negative']:.0%} complaints, "
                  f"{mix['request']:.0%} requests (raw: {card['raw_mix']['positive']:.0%} / "
                  f"{card['raw_mix']['negative']:.0%} / {card['raw_mix']['request']:.0%})",
                  f"Indices (1.0 = as expected): complaints {card['complaint_index']['index']}, "
                  f"praise {card['praise_index']['index']}, requests {card['request_index']['index']}", ""]
    for c, title in [("positive", "Why customers like it"), ("negative", "Why customers complain"),
                     ("request", "What customers ask for")]:
        fam = card["reasons"][c]["families"]
        if fam:
            lines.append(f"**{title}:** " + "; ".join(f"{k} ({v})" for k, v in fam.items()))
    if card["by_model"]:
        lines.append("**By model:** " + " | ".join(
            f"{b['group']}: {b['verdict']} (idx {b['complaint_index']}, n={b['n_comments']})" for b in card["by_model"]))
    if card["by_engine"]:
        lines.append("**By engine:** " + " | ".join(
            f"{b['group']}: {b['verdict']} (idx {b['complaint_index']}, n={b['n_comments']})" for b in card["by_engine"]))
    if card["survey"]:
        lines.append("**US survey cross-check:** " + " | ".join(
            f"{s['attribute']} {s['model']}: top-2 {s['top2_box']:.0%}, bottom-3 {s['bottom3_box']:.1%}"
            for s in card["survey"]))
    if card["options"]:
        lines.append("**Price list (DE, July 2026):** " + " | ".join(
            f"{o['model']}: {o['tier'].replace('_', ' ')} (standard {o['n_standard']}/{o['n_variants']}, "
            f"optional {o['n_optional']}/{o['n_variants']} variants"
            + (f", from EUR {o['price_min_eur']:,.0f}" if o["price_min_eur"] else "") + ")"
            for o in card["options"]))
    lines.append("")
    marks = {"positive": "+", "negative": "-", "request": "?"}
    for c, qs in card["quotes"].items():
        for qd in qs:
            text = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", qd["text"])
            lines.append(f"  {marks[c]} \"{text[:240]}\" ({qd['model']}, {qd['source']}, {qd['reason']})")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def text_card(ctx: Context, comment: str, models=None) -> dict:
    """Classify a new comment and attach verdicts for the feature(s) it mentions."""
    from .classifier import predict
    pred = predict([comment], models=models)[0]
    features = [f for f, p in pred.get("feature", []) if f in ctx.features.index]
    return {"comment": comment, "prediction": pred,
            "cards": [ctx.feature_card(f) for f in features[:2]]}


def load_context() -> Context:
    """Load processed tables (run `build` first)."""
    p = config.PROCESSED_DIR
    labels = pd.read_csv(p / "labels.csv")
    comments = pd.read_csv(p / "comments.csv", keep_default_na=False, na_values=[""])   # keep texts like "None"
    comments[["text", "text_model"]] = comments[["text", "text_model"]].fillna("")
    for col in ["feedback_types", "sentiments", "domains", "features"]:
        comments[col] = comments[col].fillna("").apply(lambda s: [x for x in s.split("|") if x])
    survey = pd.read_csv(p / "survey_us_summary.csv") if (p / "survey_us_summary.csv").exists() else None
    return Context(labels, comments, survey, load_catalog())


CATALOG_TABLES = ["variants", "price_specs", "technical", "option_items", "fitment", "packages", "page_stats",
                  "feature_option_links", "feature_fitment", "feature_fitment_summary", "feature_fitment_by_engine",
                  "feature_specs"]


def load_catalog() -> dict:
    """Parsed price-list tables written by `build` (empty dict if not built)."""
    p = config.PROCESSED_DIR
    return {t: pd.read_csv(p / f"catalog_{t}.csv") for t in CATALOG_TABLES if (p / f"catalog_{t}.csv").exists()}
"""Command line entry point: python -m bmw_feedback <command>

    build     raw Excel/PDF -> data/processed/*.csv, reports/data_quality.json, scorecards
    train     evaluate + fit text classifiers -> reports/classifier_metrics.json, models/
    figures   regenerate reports/figures/*.png
    export    JSON row files for the interactive dashboard -> data/processed/dashboard/
    verdict   PM verdict for a feature (--feature) or a new comment (--text)
    serve     API + web app (Product Decision Studio) on http://127.0.0.1:8000
    all       build + train + figures
"""

import argparse
import json
import sys

import pandas as pd

from . import clean, config, load, scoring, taxonomy


def _save_list_columns(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    out = df.copy()
    for col in ["feedback_types", "sentiments", "domains", "features"]:
        out[col] = out[col].apply("|".join)
    return out


def cmd_build(_args=None) -> None:
    config.PROCESSED_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    config.REPORTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    print("Loading raw feedback ...")
    raw = load.load_feedback()
    labels, comments, quality = clean.build_tables(raw)
    labels.to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "labels.csv", index=False)
    _save_list_columns(comments).to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "comments.csv", index=False)
    print(f"  {len(labels):,} label rows, {len(comments):,} comments "
          f"({quality['comments_by_label_status']})")

    print("Loading survey, sales ...")
    sales = load.load_sales()
    sales.to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "sales.csv", index=False)
    weights = clean.market_weights(labels, sales)
    weights.to_csv(config.REPORTS_DIR / "market_representativeness.csv", index=False)
    load.load_survey_cn_eu().to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "survey_cn_eu.csv", index=False)
    survey_us = load.load_survey_us()
    survey_us.to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "survey_us.csv", index=False)
    load.summarise_survey_us(survey_us).to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "survey_us_summary.csv", index=False)

    print("Parsing option-list PDFs ...")
    from . import option_catalog
    cat = option_catalog.build_catalog()
    quality["option_catalog"] = option_catalog.validate(cat)
    links = option_catalog.match_features(cat)
    fitment = option_catalog.feature_fitment(links, cat)
    tables = {**cat, "feature_option_links": links, "feature_fitment": fitment,
              "feature_fitment_summary": option_catalog.fitment_summary(fitment),
              "feature_fitment_by_engine": option_catalog.fitment_summary(fitment, ("feature", "model", "engine")),
              "feature_specs": option_catalog.spec_context(cat)}
    for name, frame in tables.items():
        frame.to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / f"catalog_{name}.csv", index=False)
    q = quality["option_catalog"]
    print(f"  {len(cat['variants'])} variants, {len(cat['option_items'])} items, {len(cat['fitment'])} fitment cells, "
          f"{len(cat['technical'])} technical values; {links['feature'].nunique()} feedback features linked")
    print(f"  checks passed: {q['glyphs_assigned']} glyphs assigned, {q['option_price_pairs_checked']} price pairs, "
          f"{q['base_prices_checked']} base prices; {len(q['source_price_anomalies'])} source anomaly")

    print("Scoring features ...")
    feats = scoring.score(labels)
    feats.to_csv(config.REPORTS_DIR / "feature_scorecard.csv", index=False)
    scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("domain",), prior_keys=()).to_csv(
        config.REPORTS_DIR / "domain_scorecard.csv", index=False)
    scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("domain", "model"), prior_keys=()).to_csv(
        config.REPORTS_DIR / "domain_by_model_scorecard.csv", index=False)
    scoring.score(labels, group_keys=("feature", "model")).to_csv(
        config.PROCESSED_DIR / "feature_by_model_scorecard.csv", index=False)
    units = scoring.feature_units(labels)
    specific = units[~units["feature"].isin(taxonomy.UMBRELLA_FEATURES)]
    quality["source_baselines_all_features"] = scoring.source_baselines(units).round(3).to_dict("index")
    quality["source_baselines_specific_features"] = scoring.source_baselines(specific).round(3).to_dict("index")
    quality["verdicts_specific_features"] = feats.loc[~feats["is_umbrella"], "verdict"].value_counts().to_dict()
    (config.REPORTS_DIR / "data_quality.json").write_text(json.dumps(quality, indent=2, default=str))
    print(f"  verdicts (specific features): {quality['verdicts_specific_features']}")


def cmd_train(_args=None) -> None:
    from . import classifier
    from .verdict import load_context
    ctx = load_context()
    print("Cross-validating classifiers ...")
    metrics = classifier.evaluate_all(ctx.comments)
    print("Fitting final models ...")
    classifier.fit_and_save(ctx.comments)
    pool = ctx.comments[ctx.comments["label_status"] != "labeled"]
    preds = classifier.predict(pool["text"].tolist())
    out = pool[["comment_id", "source", "model", "label_status", "text"]].copy()
    out["pred_feedback_types"] = ["|".join(f for f, _ in p["feedback_type"]) for p in preds]
    out["pred_domains"] = ["|".join(d for d, _ in p["domain"]) for p in preds]
    out["pred_top_feature"] = [p["feature"][0][0] for p in preds]
    out["pred_top_feature_p"] = [p["feature"][0][1] for p in preds]
    out.to_csv(config.PROCESSED_DIR / "unlabeled_predictions.csv", index=False)
    metrics["unlabeled_pool"] = {
        "n": int(len(out)),
        "pred_feedback_type_counts": out["pred_feedback_types"].str.split("|").explode().value_counts().to_dict(),
        "pred_domain_counts": out["pred_domains"].str.split("|").explode().value_counts().to_dict(),
    }
    classifier.save_metrics(metrics, config.REPORTS_DIR / "classifier_metrics.json")
    print(f"  saved models to {config.MODELS_DIR.relative_to(config.ROOT)}/ and metrics to reports/")

    print("Option-list ablations ...")
    from . import risk_model
    p = config.PROCESSED_DIR
    fit_by_engine = pd.read_csv(p / "catalog_feature_fitment_by_engine.csv")
    variants = pd.read_csv(p / "catalog_variants.csv")
    fitment = pd.read_csv(p / "catalog_fitment.csv")
    covered = set(map(tuple, fitment[["model", "variant"]].drop_duplicates()
                      .merge(variants[["model", "variant", "engine"]])[["model", "engine"]].drop_duplicates().values))
    units = risk_model.unit_frame(ctx.labels, fit_by_engine, variants, fitment)
    ablation = {
        "complaint_risk_ebm": risk_model.evaluate(units),
        "poor_value_check": risk_model.value_check(units, ctx.labels),
        "feature_classifier_fitment": classifier.fitment_ablation(ctx.comments, fit_by_engine, covered),
    }
    risk_model.fit_and_save(units)
    classifier.save_reranker(ablation["feature_classifier_fitment"], ctx.comments)
    ablation["complaint_risk_ebm"]["production_inputs"] = risk_model.CONTEXT
    ablation["complaint_risk_ebm"]["audit_only_inputs"] = risk_model.CONTEXT + risk_model.PDF
    ablation["complaint_risk_ebm"]["global_production"] = risk_model.global_explanation(risk_model.load())
    ablation["complaint_risk_ebm"]["global_audit_with_pdf"] = risk_model.global_explanation(risk_model.load(audit=True))
    (config.REPORTS_DIR / "model_ablation.json").write_text(json.dumps(ablation, indent=2, default=str))
    e = ablation["complaint_risk_ebm"]
    for k in ("all_features", "linked_features_only"):
        v = e[k]["variants"]
        print(f"  complaint EBM ({k}): AUC context {v['context_only']['auc_mean']:.3f} -> +PDF "
              f"{v['context_plus_pdf']['auc_mean']:.3f} (gain {e[k]['pdf_auc_gain_mean']:+.4f})")
    f = ablation["feature_classifier_fitment"]
    print(f"  feature classifier top-1 (linked): car prior {f['variants']['text_plus_car_prior']['top1_hit_linked']:.4f}"
          f" -> +fitment {f['variants']['text_plus_car_prior_plus_fitment']['top1_hit_linked']:.4f}"
          f" (McNemar p={f['mcnemar_linked']['p_value']})")


def cmd_figures(_args=None) -> None:
    from . import figures
    figures.make_all()


def cmd_export(_args=None) -> None:
    from .export import export_dashboard
    export_dashboard()


def cmd_verdict(args) -> None:
    from .verdict import load_context, render_markdown, text_card
    ctx = load_context()
    if args.list:
        cols = ["feature", "domain", "verdict", "confidence", "n_comments", "index_negative", "requested"]
        table = ctx.features.reset_index()[cols]
        table = table[table["verdict"] != "Not enough data"].round(2)
        print(table.to_string(index=False))
        return
    if args.text:
        result = text_card(ctx, args.text)
        if args.json:
            print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str))
            return
        p = result["prediction"]
        print(f"Comment classified as: {', '.join(f'{t} ({s:.0%})' for t, s in p['feedback_type'])}")
        print(f"Domain(s): {', '.join(f'{d} ({s:.0%})' for d, s in p['domain'])}")
        print(f"Top features: {', '.join(f'{f} ({s:.0%})' for f, s in p['feature'])}\n")
        for card in result["cards"]:
            print(render_markdown(card), "\n")
        return
    feature = ctx.resolve(args.feature or "")
    if feature is None:
        print(f"No feature matches {args.feature!r}. Try `--list` to see all features.")
        sys.exit(1)
    card = ctx.feature_card(feature)
    print(json.dumps(card, indent=2, default=str) if args.json else render_markdown(card))


def cmd_serve(args) -> None:
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run("bmw_feedback.api:app", host=args.host, port=args.port, reload=False)


def cmd_all(args) -> None:
    cmd_build(args)
    cmd_train(args)
    cmd_figures(args)


def main(argv=None) -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m bmw_feedback", description=__doc__,
                                     formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)
    sub.add_parser("build").set_defaults(func=cmd_build)
    sub.add_parser("train").set_defaults(func=cmd_train)
    sub.add_parser("figures").set_defaults(func=cmd_figures)
    sub.add_parser("export").set_defaults(func=cmd_export)
    sub.add_parser("all").set_defaults(func=cmd_all)
    sv = sub.add_parser("serve", help="run the API + web app (frontend/dist) on http://HOST:PORT")
    sv.add_argument("--host", default="127.0.0.1")
    sv.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=8000)
    sv.set_defaults(func=cmd_serve)
    v = sub.add_parser("verdict", help="verdict for a feature or a new comment")
    v.add_argument("--feature", "-f", help="feature name or alias, e.g. 'head-up display', 'carplay'")
    v.add_argument("--text", "-t", help="a new customer comment to classify")
    v.add_argument("--list", action="store_true", help="list all features with a verdict")
    v.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="machine-readable output")
    v.set_defaults(func=cmd_verdict)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    args.func(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Three-level category taxonomy for BMW customer feedback.

Level 1  domain   - 11 product areas a PM owns (hand-curated below)
Level 2  feature  - the VFC level-2 label shipped in the data (226 values)
Level 3  reason   - the VFC level-3 label, grouped into reason families

This mirrors the old Demandra abstraction ladder (E-Class -> +Manufacturer ->
+Feature cluster): verdicts are most robust at the domain level and most
actionable at the feature + reason level.
"""

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Level 1: domain -> VFC level-2 features
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
DOMAIN_FEATURES = {
    "Drivetrain & Performance": [
        "Drivetrain", "Transmission", "Engine acoustics / engine sound",
        "Automatic engine start-stop function (MSA)", "Launch Control", "Shift paddle",
        "Operate selector lever", "Starting engine", "Start engine/switch on drive readiness",
        "Exhaust system", "Fuel tank", "Fuel filler flap , open / close", "Cooling",
}

DOMAINS = list(DOMAIN_FEATURES)

# Short labels for charts
DOMAIN_SHORT = {
    "Drivetrain & Performance": "Drivetrain",
    "Chassis & Driving Dynamics": "Chassis & dynamics",
    "EV Charging & Range": "EV charging & range",
    "Driver Assistance & Safety": "Assistance & safety",
    "Infotainment & HMI": "Infotainment & HMI",
    "Connected Apps & Digital Services": "Connected apps",
    "Seats, Comfort & Climate": "Seats & climate",
    "Interior Design & Storage": "Interior & storage",
    "Exterior Design & Body": "Exterior & body",
    "Doors, Access & Keys": "Doors & access",
    "Ownership & Service": "Ownership & service",
}

# Umbrella labels: generic, car-level labels. Annotators file most praise here
# ('Exterior design' has 391 comments and 0 complaints) while complaints land on
# specific components. Specific features are therefore compared only with other
# specific features (see scoring.py). Chosen by name, not by sentiment.

# Features that only exist on electrified cars (used to flag label noise on ICE)
EV_ONLY_FEATURES = set(DOMAIN_FEATURES["EV Charging & Range"])

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Level 3: VFC level-3 reason -> reason family (the "why" shown to the PM)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
REASON_FAMILIES = {

                                "Installation and set-up: difficult", "Accidental triggering"],
    "Cannot be switched off": ["Permanent switch-off not possible", "Switch off not possible"],
    "Inaccurate information": ["Information / accuracy insufficient",
                               "Information / Accuracy insufficient (electric range)"],
    # negative: defects
    "Malfunction / software fault": ["Malfunction", "Connection fault", "Blank / frozen screen",
                                     "Communication fault", "Reception quality not OK",
                                     "Warning / notification active", "Installation: fault"],
    "Battery drain": ["Battery discharge", "Capacity loss"],
    "Build quality / damage": ["Damage", "Fitting fault", "Workmanship does not appeal", "Leak",
                               "Leak: water ingress/condensation", "Leak: air", "Condensation",
                               "Cavity sealant: wax residue", "Locking, detent: fault", "Dirty contamination",

    out.columns = [f"{a}_{b}" for a, b in out.columns]
    out["n_units"] = obs.sum(axis=1)
    out["n_comments"] = units.groupby(keys)["comment_id"].nunique()
    return out


def score(labels: pd.DataFrame, group_keys=("feature",), prior_keys=("domain",)) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Score every group (default: feature) with indices, intervals and a verdict.

    group_keys can include 'model' or 'engine' for breakdowns; the prior is
    then taken at (domain + the same extra keys).
    """
    units = feature_units(labels)
    group_keys, prior_keys = list(group_keys), list(prior_keys)
    feature_level = "feature" in group_keys
    peers = units[~units["feature"].isin(taxonomy.UMBRELLA_FEATURES)] if feature_level else units
    base = source_baselines(peers)
    extra = [k for k in group_keys if k not in ("feature", "domain")]
    prior_keys = prior_keys + extra

    g = _observed_expected(units, group_keys, base)
    if prior_keys:
        p = _observed_expected(peers, prior_keys, base)
        for c in SENTIMENTS:
            p[f"prior_{c}"] = (p[f"obs_{c}"] + 1) / (p[f"exp_{c}"] + 1)
    else:                                   # top level: prior is "as expected"
        p = pd.DataFrame({f"prior_{c}": [1.0] for c in SENTIMENTS})

    if "domain" not in group_keys:
        dom = units.drop_duplicates(group_keys)[group_keys + ["domain"]].set_index(group_keys)["domain"]
        g = g.join(dom)
    g = g.reset_index()
    if prior_keys:
        g = g.merge(p[[f"prior_{c}" for c in SENTIMENTS]].reset_index(), on=prior_keys, how="left")
    else:
        g = g.merge(p, how="cross")

    if feature_level:
        g["is_umbrella"] = g["feature"].isin(taxonomy.UMBRELLA_FEATURES)
    k = config.PRIOR_STRENGTH
    overall = peers["sentiment"].value_counts(normalize=True).reindex(SENTIMENTS)
    for c in SENTIMENTS:
        g[f"index_{c}"] = (g[f"obs_{c}"] + k * g[f"prior_{c}"]) / (g[f"exp_{c}"] + k)
        g[f"ci_low_{c}"], g[f"ci_high_{c}"] = _byar_interval(g[f"obs_{c}"], g[f"exp_{c}"])
        g[f"raw_share_{c}"] = g[f"obs_{c}"] / g["n_units"]
    # Channel-adjusted shares: overall share x index, renormalised to sum to 1
    adj = pd.DataFrame({c: overall[c] * g[f"index_{c}"] for c in SENTIMENTS})
    adj = adj.div(adj.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
    for c in SENTIMENTS:
        g[f"adj_share_{c}"] = adj[c]

    # Which kind of 'bad'? Defect (engineering / quality) vs Difficult to Use (UX)
    neg = units[units["sentiment"] == "negative"]
    kind = pd.crosstab([neg[k_] for k_ in group_keys], neg["feedback_type"])
    kind = kind.reindex(columns=["Defect", "Difficult to Use"], fill_value=0)
    kind.columns = ["n_defect", "n_difficult_to_use"]
    g = g.merge(kind.reset_index(), on=group_keys, how="left")
    g[["n_defect", "n_difficult_to_use"]] = g[["n_defect", "n_difficult_to_use"]].fillna(0).astype(int)

    g["verdict"] = g.apply(_verdict, axis=1)
    g["confidence"] = pd.cut(g["n_comments"], [0, config.MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_VERDICT - 1, 29, 99, np.inf],
                             labels=["insufficient", "low", "medium", "high"]).astype(str)
    g["requested"] = ((g["n_comments"] >= config.MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_VERDICT)
                      & (g["index_request"] >= config.REQUEST_INDEX) & (g["ci_low_request"] > 1))
    order = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(VERDICTS)}
    return g.sort_values(["verdict", "n_comments"], key=lambda s: s.map(order) if s.name == "verdict" else -s)


def _verdict(row) -> str:
    """Bad / Good need the 95% interval to exclude 'as expected' (index 1.0);
    the 'Leaning' tiers only need the point estimate past a softer threshold."""
    neg, pos = row["index_negative"], row["index_positive"]
    if row["n_comments"] < config.MIN_MENTIONS_FOR_VERDICT:
        return "Not enough data"
    if neg >= config.BAD_INDEX and row["ci_low_negative"] > 1:
        return "Bad"
    if neg <= config.GOOD_NEG_INDEX and row["ci_high_negative"] < 1 and pos >= 1:
        return "Good"
    if neg >= config.LEAN_BAD_INDEX:
        return "Leaning bad"
    if neg <= config.LEAN_GOOD_NEG_INDEX and pos >= 1:
        return "Leaning good"
    return "Mixed"


def bad_kind(row) -> str:
    """'defect-led' / 'usability-led' / 'mixed' for the negative mentions of a feature."""
    total = row["n_defect"] + row["n_difficult_to_use"]
    if total == 0:
        return "none"
    share = row["n_defect"] / total
    return "defect-led" if share >= 0.6 else "usability-led" if share <= 0.4 else "defects and usability"


def reason_breakdown(labels: pd.DataFrame, feature: str, top: int = 3) -> dict:
    """Top reason families per sentiment for one feature (counts of comments)."""
    lab = labels[(labels["feature"] == feature) & labels["is_feature_label"]]
    out = {}
    for c in SENTIMENTS:
        sub = lab[lab["sentiment"] == c].drop_duplicates(["comment_id", "reason_family"])
        vc = sub["reason_family"].value_counts().head(top)
        detail = sub["reason"].value_counts().head(top)
        out[c] = {"families": vc.to_dict(), "reasons": detail.to_dict()}
    return out


def representative_quotes(labels: pd.DataFrame, comments: pd.DataFrame, feature: str, per_sentiment: int = 2) -> dict:
    """Short, single-topic cleaned quotes for each sentiment of a feature."""
    lab = labels[labels["feature"] == feature].drop_duplicates(["comment_id", "sentiment"])
    merged = lab.merge(comments[["comment_id", "text", "n_labels", "n_words"]], on="comment_id")
    merged = merged[(merged["n_words"] >= 6)]
    merged["focus"] = (merged["n_labels"] == 1).astype(int)
    merged["len_penalty"] = (merged["text"].str.len() - 140).abs()
    out = {}
    for c in SENTIMENTS:
        sub = merged[merged["sentiment"] == c].sort_values(["focus", "len_penalty"], ascending=[False, True])
        sub = sub.drop_duplicates("text").head(per_sentiment)
        out[c] = [{"comment_id": r.comment_id, "model": r.model, "source": r.source, "reason": r.reason,
                   "text": r.text} for r in sub.itertuples()]
    return out


def survey_crosscheck(survey_us: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Map US survey attributes onto feedback features (feature, model, top2, bottom3)."""
    rows = []
    for attr, feats in taxonomy.US_SURVEY_TO_FEATURES.items():
        for f in feats:
            rows.append({"survey_attribute": attr, "feature": f})
    m = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return m.merge(survey_us, left_on="survey_attribute", right_on="attribute").drop(columns="attribute")

# PM Idea Evaluator: knowledge graph + three-agent evaluation

Date: 2026-10-10. Status: approved by the user ("implement approach A and do everything").

## Goal

A BMW product manager types a feature idea. The app answers, per series (F70, G60, G70) and market (EU, US, CN, RoW),
whether to pursue it, explains why in plain language, and proves that every sentence comes from the processed data
or a trained model. The frontend has one job: evaluating that idea.

## Decisions taken with the user

| Topic | Decision |
|---|---|
| Approach | A: engine-grounded fact bundle. The LLM never computes a number. |
| LLM provider | OpenAI, key in `OPENAI_API_KEY` (env or repo-root `.env`, git-ignored) |
| Models | Retriever + verifier: `gpt-6-luna`. Explainer: `gpt-6-terra`. Each overridable by env var; checked against the account's model list at first use and never silently replaced. |
| PM input | Free text. The retriever extracts an `IdeaSpec`; the PM confirms or edits it before evaluation. |
| Verifier failure | One rewrite with the failures fed back, then unsupported claims are removed and listed. |
| Page content | Explanation, verification report, series x market matrix, evidence graph, decision record + policy. |
| Old pages | Page files deleted; their API endpoints stay (tests and the evaluation use them). |
| Design | Tokens measured on bmw.de (crawl 2026-10-10). Buttons/inputs 3px as on bmw.de; content cards rounder (12-16px) by user choice; floating panels 8px + shadow. |
| Brand assets | Official BMW logo SVGs and BMW Type Next woff2 fetched from bmw.de for local use; git-ignored; fetch script committed; Barlow is the fallback. |
| No key | Retrieval falls back to rules + TF-IDF and is labelled as such; evaluation works; the explanation panel says it is unavailable (no template prose). |

## Architecture

```
build:   processed CSVs + models/ + reports/*.json --graph/build.py--> data/processed/knowledge_graph.json
                                                                       data/processed/graph_schema.json
request: idea --Agent 1 Retriever--> IdeaSpec (validated) --PM confirms-->
         DecisionEngine.evaluate (unchanged maths) --> FactBundle + evidence subgraph   (rendered immediately)
         --Agent 2 Explainer--> claims citing fact IDs --Agent 3 Verifier--> retry once --> strip  (fills in)
```

## Knowledge graph (networkx MultiDiGraph, node-link JSON)

Every node: `id` (`type:key`, keys are the source names), `type`, `label`, attributes, `prov` (table + key, or file + page).
Every edge: `rel`, attributes, endpoints that must exist (the builder refuses to create nodes implicitly).

| Node type | Count source | Provenance |
|---|---|---|
| Series (F70, G60, G70, G68 survey-only) | config | config.py |
| Variant | catalog_variants.csv | `<series>_OptionList.PDF` page |
| Market | 4 | config.py |
| SalesVolume (series group x market x year) | sales.csv | sales_volumes.xlsx |
| Domain | taxonomy (11) | reports/domain_scorecard.csv |
| Feature | feature_scorecard.csv (224) | reports/feature_scorecard.csv |
| Reason, ReasonFamily | labels.csv (84, 21) | taxonomy.py |
| Comment | comments.csv (10,128) | `<series>_feedback_hackathon.xlsx` |
| SurveyAttribute, SurveyScore | survey_cn_eu.csv, survey_us_summary.csv | customer_studies.xlsx |
| OptionItem, Package, TechSpec | catalog_*.csv | PDF page |
| FitmentSummary (feature x series) | catalog_feature_fitment_summary.csv | derived from the PDFs |
| VerdictCell (feature; feature x series; feature x series x market; domain) | scoring.score | model output |
| ModelArtifact (3 classifiers, complaint EBM, fitment re-ranker) | reports/*.json, models/ | model output |
| EBMTerm | model_ablation.json | model output |
| Caveat | computed from the data (e.g. "G70 tables cover 4 of 7 variants") | derived |

Relations: IN_DOMAIN, MENTIONS {sentiment, feedback_type, reason}, ABOUT, FROM_MARKET, HAS_REASON {sentiment, count},
IN_FAMILY, MEASURES, SCORES_ATTRIBUTE, FOR_SERIES, IN_MARKET, LISTED_FOR, FITTED_ON {status, price_eur},
VARIANT_OF, LINKED_TO {matched_keyword}, HAS_SPEC, SPEC_OF, INCLUDES, FITMENT_OF, ON_SERIES, HAS_SALES,
SCORES, PREDICTED_AS {p, model}, TERM_OF, CONTRIBUTES {bin, score}, QUALIFIES, LONG_WHEELBASE_OF.

The build asserts counts against the source tables (features, domains, variants, items, fitment rows, links,
comments, feature labels, specs) and fails loudly on a mismatch.

## Agents (bmw_feedback/agents)

1. Retriever (`gpt-6-luna`). Candidates come from code only: alias/name/fuzzy matches and the trained feature
   classifier (`DecisionEngine.resolve_idea`) plus a semantic index over feature documents (OpenAI
   `text-embedding-3-small`, cached; TF-IDF without a key). The LLM picks among candidate names and extracts
   series, markets, move (fix_existing, make_standard, new_option, price_change, introduce_on_series, unspecified)
   and a proposed price. Output is validated by `IdeaSpec` (features must be candidates, enums enforced, price > 0,
   at most 3 features). On a validation error the errors are fed back for up to 2 retries.
2. Explainer (`gpt-6-terra`). Receives the `FactBundle` (facts with stable IDs, deterministic statements, values,
   provenance) and writes an `Explanation`: headline, customer evidence, market view, price and equipment, risks and
   caveats, next steps. Every claim cites fact IDs.
3. Verifier (rules first, then `gpt-6-luna`). Per claim: citations present; cited IDs exist; every number matches a
   cited value at the displayed precision (percent forms included); recommendation and verdict labels match cited
   values; quoted text is a substring of a cited comment; series and markets named are in the cited facts' scope;
   then an LLM entailment check for what rules cannot see. Failures go back to the explainer once; anything still
   failing is removed and listed in the report.

## API (added; existing endpoints unchanged)

`GET /api/agent/status`, `POST /api/agent/interpret`, `POST /api/agent/evaluate`, `POST /api/agent/explain`,
`GET /api/graph/schema`, `GET /api/graph/node/{id}`.

## Frontend

One route. bmw.de layout patterns: transparent nav over a dark hero, sticky in-page tab bar with active underline,
key-figure rows (light label over light value) with 12px grey source notes, full-bleed dark bands. Sections: idea
input -> extracted IdeaSpec (editable) -> key figures -> explanation with citation chips and verification marks ->
series x market matrix with evidence panel -> price ladder -> evidence graph (cytoscape, instance and schema views,
node inspector) -> verification report -> decision policy + decision record.

## Testing

pytest with a fake LLM client (no network): graph counts and integrity, IdeaSpec validation and retry, rules
fallback, verifier catching a fabricated number, a wrong series, a misquote, and the retry-then-strip loop; API
status/interpret/evaluate/explain. Frontend: `tsc` build plus a Playwright screenshot pass.
